Both Function [[40]] and Meaning [[41]] play a unique role in Systems [[38]] especially as examined in Lzahlia's Systems-Theory [[27]]

While function is mechanical and observable, meaning is immaterial [[25]]; non-observable. Paradoxically, meaning is experientially necessary [[35]] while being unquantifiable (no empirical logic) yet fundamental. Meaning also requires function, just as much as Function requires a meaning. This is the primary "Cybernetic" aspect of the entanglement; both are reliant on one another.

The primary idea in this cluster, is studying the necessary Continuum [[50]] between Meaning and Function as a dynamic Equillibria

Meaning cannot merely be computed [[30]]; neither synergistic-emergence, or machinistic-processes. Meaning appears to exist in a space outside of space-time; suggesting a "Logos" or "The Word" [[9]] as a fundamental order of all things. Studied further in [[2]]

Among "Meaning" and "Function" is a Unifying "Gravity" force, or "The Logos." From the Logos, we also study Equillibria [[]] and Weight [[]] (Priority, Influence, Importance, Significance)" Propositionally; nothing within a system can "self-organize, self-classify or self-prioritize." Systems of values [[]] are fundamentally contextual; living outside a system.
